content: Avoid using antacids that contain magnesium trisilicate while taking this medication. The dosage and duration of this medication are determined based on your specific medical condition and your response to treatment. To achieve the best therapeutic effect, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals. If you are using this medication to prevent an infection, follow your doctor’s instructions precisely. Do not skip doses or discontinue the medication without consulting your doctor. If you are taking this medication to treat an infection, continue taking it for the full prescribed duration, even if your symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, or headache. Taking this medication with food can help reduce nausea. It may also cause your urine to appear dark yellow or brown, which is generally harmless. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. However, this medication may rarely cause serious, potentially fatal lung problems. These lung issues may occur within the first month of treatment or after long-term use (typically six months or longer). In rare cases, this medication may cause severe liver disease, blood disorders, or nerve problems. It may also lead to a serious intestinal condition caused by the bacteria Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may result in oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection (such as oral or vaginal fungal infections). Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. This is not a comprehensive list of potential side effects. If you are in the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Before taking nitrofurantoin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Nitrofurantoin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines (such as the typhoid vaccine). During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It should not be used near or at the time of delivery (weeks 38–42 of pregnancy) due to the risk of harm to the newborn, such as a specific blood disorder (hemolytic anemia). This medication passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on nursing infants younger than one month old or infants with a specific genetic condition (G6PD deficiency). Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests (such as specific urine glucose tests), potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as complete blood counts, kidney and liver function tests, and urine cultures) should be performed while you are taking this medication. Be sure to attend all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
